definition: A large, publicly available repository of web-crawled data, widely used as a raw data source for pretraining large language models.
details: Common Crawl provides petabytes of web page data collected over many years, and is typically filtered, deduplicated, and cleaned extensively before being used in LLM pretraining pipelines.
story: Think of a historian sorting through boxes of letters, building a picture of an era one sentence at a time. Every machine is shaped by what it was shown, so someone has to choose that material with care. The examples a machine reads become the world it believes in. The words a model reads become the world it believes in. That care with the raw material is Common Crawl.
